description:
## Destination

A design spec for the **build service** turnkey ships as a product: building blocks that any turnkey-managed repo on GitHub assembles to get Google-like incremental builds and tests on every machine (CI, laptops) without trusting PRs or developer machines. The backend is one service with two faces over shared storage — REAPI (content store, action cache, Execute with a Nix-programmable base image) and a Nix binary cache — deployed on Cloud Run and scaling to zero. The map is done when every block's interface and every trust rule is decided in `docs/specs/build-service.md` (plus ADRs and CONTEXT.md terms), and the build work is carved into execution epics (turnkey-lbe among them).

## Notes

- **Planning only** (wayfinder default): tickets produce decisions, not deliverables. Exception: ticket "Record the trust rule…" writes the ADR/glossary.
- **Living spec**: each resolved ticket adds or updates its section of `docs/specs/build-service.md`; write an ADR in `docs/adr/` when a choice is hard to reverse, surprising, and a real trade-off. Use /domain-modeling for CONTEXT.md terms, /grilling for grilling tickets, /research for research tickets (findings under `docs/research/`), /codebase-design for block seams, /prototype when "how would it behave" is the question.
- Background reading: `docs/research/remote-execution-and-caching.md` (gaps G0–G11, key hygiene), `docs/research/local-re-api-servers.md`, ADR 0001 (runner-recorded test caching), ADR 0002 (pinned buck2 release).
- VCS is jj; repo rules in CLAUDE.md apply.
- **Settled while charting (2026-09-26):**
  - Product feature, not turnkey-CI ops: turnkey ships composable building blocks; turnkey's own repo is the first assembly (dogfood).
  - **Trust rule — clients submit work, never results.** Clients may upload content-store blobs (hash-verified) and submit Nix *derivations*; only the executor writes action results, and only the service's Nix builder produces store paths (built in the Nix sandbox, signed by the service key). The Nix cache therefore needs no scopes.
  - Trust root = the build service and its operators. Every client (laptop, CI runner, same-repo or fork PR) is untrusted; the code under build is irrelevant to integrity. Fork PRs from non-members need approval before anything runs (cost, not integrity). Confidentiality is not a goal: repo readers may read its artifacts.
  - Remote execution is the core (reverses the research note's "cache only first"). Local execution remains only for what the service can't run (darwin actions, offline).
  - Executor results are **shared across everyone** (Google model) — falling back to per-trust-level services writing into requester scopes if Cloud Run can't isolate successive actions on one instance.
  - Never promote a PR's results into a trusted namespace.
  - **Programmable base image** = one generic executor image; per action, the store paths it names (absolute `/nix/store` symlink targets in the input tree, plus closure roots in a platform property) are fetched from the Nix cache (built by the service if missing), cached per instance, mounted read-only into the action sandbox.
  - **Scale to zero is a hard requirement**: an idle deployment costs its stored bytes only. niks3 needs Postgres → explore refactoring it onto a scale-to-zero store.
  - GCP first; clients speak only REAPI and the Nix binary-cache protocol, so the provider stays inside the service.
  - Where the buck2 client runs: GitHub Actions runners (default), laptops, and a service-owned client host (e.g. Cloud Run job) for fork PRs and developer-requested builds.
  - Triggers: GitHub events, plus developer-requested builds (later phase).
  - Platforms: design covers Linux and darwin; Linux executor first, darwin executor later.
  - Glossary: adopt **Build service**, **Executor**, **Client**, **Client-computed result**; **Scope** held until "Which results are shared…"; "Landing build" retired.

## Decisions so far

- [Can niks3 run on a metadata store that scales to zero?](turnkey-wit.4) — no; don't port it. The Nix cache is a GCS bucket written only by the service's builder through Nix's own S3 store; public reads go straight to GCS or a CDN, private ones through a stateless read proxy; GC is a scheduled Cloud Run job with a GCS lock file, and there is no database. Fallback: unmodified niks3 on Neon. Findings: docs/research/niks3-scale-to-zero.md on bookmark research/niks3-scale-to-zero (d8be99d2).
- [Which REAPI implementations or components fit a request-driven executor?](turnkey-wit.2) — none as shipped. Build on Buildbarn's Go libraries (hash check on upload, `UpdateActionResult` denied to clients, cache entries with missing blobs refused, scheduler-less runner) and write our own `Execute` handler and GCS storage layer. The pinned buck2 uses one `Execute` stream per action and never calls `WaitExecution`. Caveats: Cloud Run caps an action at 60 min with no resume, and GCS needs a cache on each instance. Findings: docs/research/request-driven-reapi-executor.md on bookmark research/request-driven-reapi-executor (cdf17416).
- [How can a client ask a remote service to build a derivation?](turnkey-wit.5) — through our own narrow gRPC "realise" API (upload the `.drv` closure and sources, Realise, Watch). A disposable builder behind it is an untrusted client of a stock `nix-daemon`; signing and upload happen outside the builder, whose cloud identity can't write to the cache. Nix has no network transport for untrusted callers (daemon protocol runs over a Unix socket, SSH or stdio). **Qualifies the trust rule**: sharing untrusted-built outputs is only as sound as the Nix sandbox (CVE-2026-39860) — see "Do we accept the sandbox-escape risk…". Findings: docs/research/remote-derivation-builds.md on bookmark research/remote-derivation-builds (e7c909ed).
- [Can Cloud Run host an REAPI executor and a Nix builder?](turnkey-wit.1) — yes as Cloud Run **services** (gRPC streaming over end-to-end HTTP/2, 60-min request cap, 8 vCPU / 32 GiB, zero idle cost), not functions; Nix builds over 60 min go to Cloud Run **jobs** (fresh instance per task). Instances are always reused; isolating successive actions depends on **Cloud Run sandboxes** (Preview since 2026-07-08), not yet verified with real actions. The Nix sandbox inside Cloud Run is doubtful (seccomp, no mounts), so builders must set `sandbox-fallback = false`. The per-instance store cache is warm-only. Findings: docs/research/cloud-run-executor.md on bookmark research/cloud-run-executor (bca53006).

## Not yet specified

- Developer-requested builds: shipping a working copy to the service (CAS upload of the tree?), and how results show up for the developer.
- A darwin executor (Mac hardware; Cloud Run is Linux only).
- Garbage collection and retention of the content store, action cache and Nix cache, in a scale-to-zero design.
- Quotas and abuse controls (fork PRs, anonymous reads) — compute costs money.
- Tests on the executor: buck2 caches remotely executed tests natively; what is left for turnkey-test-runner and `test_caching.bzl` (local/darwin tests only?).
- Observability: hit rates, per-build cost, where a hit came from.
- The service-owned client host for fork PRs.
- Carving the spec into execution epics, and rewriting turnkey-lbe's blocked children.

## Out of scope

- Distributing turnkey's own tools through the `firefly-turnkey` Cachix: unrelated to consumers' build artifacts.
- Target determination (choosing affected tests before building): orthogonal to where results live and who writes them; a separate effort.
title: Incremental builds everywhere for turnkey repos on GitHub
